description: NUMBERING NOTE: the rapport fixes the Thera list as Zb 1-4, Zg 5, Zb 6 (House of the Ladies, inedit), THE 7-12 (6 [?] tablet fragments, Delta 18a, 1993, inedits), Zb 13 (Xeste 2 pithos); it REJECTS Karnava's scheme (Michailidou's Room Delta-3 amphora fragment - signs 'ne semblent pas constituer une veritable inscription' - as Zb 6, shifting old 6-9 to 7-10, Xeste 2 = Zb 11); Michailidou's proposed readings for that fragment: A 318-AB 08 / 41 / 27 (all dotted)
publication: Michailidou 2000-2001 [2002], Indications of Literacy in Bronze Age Thera, Minos 35-36, 12-15; Karnava in Horizon (2008), 378
notes: BOOKKEEPING/DIVERGENCE row: silver Thera IDs are a MIXED BAG (THEZb5 AND THEZg5; THEZb6 AND THEZb7; ad-hoc THEfr.1-3/THEtab.4-5; Del Freo's Zb13 + editors' Zb15) - divergence-register candidate

description: INEDITS: six new vase inscriptions found 1997-2005 in ceramic material from the temple of Athena; local clay, engraved before firing, very small fragments of one or two signs: Zb 2 ]AB 56-[ (pithos), Zb 3 ]AB 41-04[ (small closed vase), Zb 4 ]AB 41[, Zb 5 ]AB 08[, Zb 6 ]AB 31[ (31 dotted), Zb 7 AB 27-[ (plus a post-firing sign resembling a ship's prow); all now dated LM IA (Zb 1 re-dated from LM IB/II to LM IA per Zurbach)
publication: To be published by Niemeier & Zurbach in Kadmos (appeared 2015 REORGANIZED as Niemeier, Del Freo & Zurbach, Kadmos 54 - see Rapport 2011-2015 row)
notes: RENUMBERED IN EDITION: 2015 publication keeps Zb 2 (AB 56-29[), Zb 3 (]AB 41-04[), suppresses old Zb 4/5/6 (isolated signs), renumbers Zb 7 -> Zb 4 (]AB 27-86[); silver has MILZb1-4 = the final 2015 state

description: NEGATIVE: Zurbach re-studied the spindle-whorls published by Schliemann 1875, in which Godart had recognized two LA inscriptions; probable dating Troy II or III and comparison with contemporary whorls identify the engraved signs as decorative motifs of a local tradition; same conclusion for vases Schmidt 2444 and 2445
publication: Zurbach 2003, Schriftahnliche Zeichen und Topferzeichen in Troia, Studia Troica 13, 115-116
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - not LA; correctly absent from silver

description: Clay reel-shaped object (h. 3.20 x diam. 2.60-2.65 cm), vertically perforated (necklace element?), five signs incised on the concave surface; found September 1996 inside 'Construction B' of a funerary complex on the Kajrjaka hill near Drama; dating uncertain; Fol & Schmitt: at least three of the five signs are LA, inscription sinistroverse, reading AB 01-51-A 301-[.]-[.] or AB 01-51-A 301-[.]-79 (01, 51, 301, 79 dotted), supported by initial AB 01-51 in KN Zf 31 and HT 95a.1; DEL FREO: published photos do not permit assessment; on the facsimile the first sign = AB 01 is 'plutot discutable'; the local-imitation conclusion is too risky (uncertain date, reading difficulties, support without Bronze-Age Aegean parallel)
publication: Fol & Schmitt 2000, A Linear A Text on a Clay Reel from Drama, South-East Bulgaria?, PZ 75, 56-62
notes: DOUBT FLAG: silver INCLUDES DRAZg1 although Del Freo treats the attribution as unassessable/doubtful; divergence-register candidate

description: Jug handle from Phylakopi (Ashmolean AE 2330), end of phase II / start of phase III (~MM III - LM I), two signs engraved after firing; Driessen: possibly LA, readable A 301-AB 27 or AB 37-27; Del Freo: AB 29 or A 314 not excluded for the second sign; since neither sign is attributable with certainty to the LA repertoire, Sherratt's conclusion is adopted ('one cannot be certain that they actually represent literate signs belonging to this - or any other - system of writing'); the classification MI Zb 3 (Karnava, Younger) is therefore 'discutable' (fn. 62)
publication: Sherratt 2000, Catalogue of Cycladic Antiquities in the Ashmolean Museum, 350-351, pl. 606, fig. 261
corpus_status: in corpus (as MIZb3); see notes (divergence/doubt flag)
notes: DOUBT FLAG: silver INCLUDES MIZb3 although the rapport declines the attribution; divergence-register candidate

description: BOOKKEEPING: the Borda-catalogue no. 9 nodule believed absent from the Pigorini collection is a photographic phantom - plate XLV juxtaposed two photographic plates on which the same nodule HT Wa 1547 appears twice (no. 8 inv. 71976 = pl. XLV:12 and no. 9 = pl. XLV:17); verified in the Museum's photo archive by Del Freo
publication: Del Freo 2002-2003, I noduli del Museo Preistorico-Etnografico 'Luigi Pigorini' provenienti da Haghia Triada, Bullettino di paletnologia italiana 93-95 (N.S. XI-XII), 53-75
notes: Phantom duplicate eliminated; HT Wa 1547 present in silver

description: NEGATIVE: cylindrical alabastron with four signs engraved after firing, three compatible with LA (Egetmeyer: first ~ A 706, second ~ A 339, fourth ~ A 304; third without parallels); origin unknown, stylistically East-Mediterranean/Cypriot, LH IIIA2 - early IIIC; signs could have been added elsewhere/later; a forgery cannot be excluded; DEL FREO: leave this graffito OUT of the LA corpus
publication: Egetmeyer & Zavadil 2004, Ein Spatbronzezeitliches Alabastron aus dem ostlichen Mittelmeerraum mit Graffito, Kadmos 43, 151-158
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - excluded from corpus; correctly absent from silver

description: PUBLICATION NOTE: the five documents announced in Rapport 2001-2005 are published by Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager with the numbering KH 97, 98, 99, Zb 1, Wc 2123; the rapport maintains the correct numbering KH 97, 99, 100, Zb 98, Wc 2123 (see Rapport 2001-2005 sub 2.2.1.5) and numbers the new 2009/2010 tablets 101 and 102 on that basis; ON THE ROUNDEL (Wc 2123) THE NEW SIGN A 373 IS ATTESTED
publication: Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, New and unpublished Linear A and Linear B inscriptions from Khania, PDIA 5, 7-22
notes: BOOKKEEPING row; all five present in silver under DEL FREO's numbering (KH97a/b, KHZb98, KH99, KH100, KHWc2123); A 373 sign-inventory addition later disputed (Rapport 2016-2021: tripod-logogram variant)

description: INEDIT: roundel found intact 2007 by Andreadaki-Vlasaki in the Katre 1 plot, a few tens of metres from Katre 10 where a 1970s LA archive was excavated; layer with local LM IIIB pottery + a few LM IB vase fragments; one face reads the logogram AB 54 (= LB TELA); fifteen impressions of a single seal on the rim; LA TELA parallels: HT 16, 20, 38, HT Wc 3019, THE 8 (and possibly TEL Zb 1, fn. 31)
publication: AR 2007-2008, 112 (preliminary); ed.pr. later Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Hallager 2018, Kadmos 57 (round-1 row)
notes: READING LATER CORRECTED: ed.pr. 2018 reads a variant of AB 61, NOT AB 54 'as previously reported' (Rapport 2016-2021, round-1 row) - the corrected item is exactly this report; present in silver

description: INEDIT: tablet fragment recording quantities of commodities, found 2009 by Andreadaki-Vlasaki in the same layer as roundel Wc 2124
publication: Ethnos online 2010-02-03; Chronique des fouilles en ligne notice 1855; ed.pr. later Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Godart 2014 (see Rapport 2011-2015 row)
notes: Numbering presupposes Del Freo's KH scheme; present in silver

description: INEDIT: tablet fragment with traces of two signs, found July 2010 by Hallager out of context in the same layer (now dated LM IIIB1) where the 2005 fragment KH 99-Hallager (= KH 100 Del Freo) was found
publication: Ed.pr. later Hallager, Tzedakis & Andreadaki-Vlazaki 2014, PDIA 7 (see Rapport 2011-2015 row)
notes: Present in silver; the layer re-dating LM IIIA -> LM IIIB1 also affects KH 100

description: PUBLISHED: the jug with four before-firing signs on the shoulder found December 1993 by Macdonald ~800 m SW of the palace (Hellenistic-kilns area), MM IIIB context (announced Rapport 1991-1995 p. 425); on Macdonald's published photo one reads rather easily the hapax AB 79-53-30-80 (cf. AB 28-79-53-30-59 in PH 6.2)
publication: Macdonald 2000, Knossos: Present and Future, in Huxley (ed.) Cretan Quests, 64, fig. 39
pages: Cretan Quests p. 64 fig. 39; rapport p. 9
notes: Reading printed in rapport (Del Freo's, from the published photo); present in silver - check silver carries AB 79-53-30-80

description: NEW: signs incised on two LM I vase fragments detected summer 2007 during pottery study of the Block C houses, including 'a sign for olive oil' (Kentro Newsletter); to be published together with a third subsequently identified fragment in the excavation report for that part of the settlement (Brogan pers. comm.)

notes: ABSENT from silver (no designations assigned); NOT resolved in Rapports 2011-2021; corpus/bronze/kentro_newsletters holds the source newsletter; Younger lists Mochlos pointers (round-1 channel)

description: RE-READING: Davis proposes AB 67 instead of the ligature AB 13+40 of the ed.pr. (Driessen 1991, ABSA 86, 146-147 fig. 22: 'AB 13et40-59-30-04'), restoring the hapax AB 67-59-30-04; parallels invoked: AB 67-59-06-41-57-09 (PE Zb 3) and ]-AB 60-67-59-06-41-[ (KH 60.1); photo-based, original not examined; Del Freo: parallels fairly convincing, re-examination needed
publication: Davis 2008, A New Reading of PK Zb 21, Kadmos 47, 55-56
notes: CONFIRMED LATER by Del Freo & Zurbach autopsy 2011-04-15 (Rapport 2011-2015 row); present in silver - check which reading silver carries

description: EDITION: Muhly & Olivier publish the complete Symi set (Za 1-3 already in GORILA V; Za 4-6 + Zb 7 previously flagged in rapports; Za 8-12 previously unpublished); readings printed in the rapport: Za 1 as GORILA V with Olivier's apparatus alternative (AB 28-01, AB 73-[[,]] 57-.[); Za 2 unchanged (AB 80, 122, A 302 now dotted); Za 3 LONGER TEXT after a join [HM 3757 (1976, 1981) + 2 frr. (1992, 2000)]: AB 08-59-28-A 301-54[...ca 8 s....].-.-.-09-77-06-41[-.-]04[...ca 10 s....]AB 41-26-04 (several dotted); Za 4: AB 08-59-28-A 301-54-57 , 57-28-48-17 (or -02) , 56-30-40 - FIRST ATTESTATION OF AB 48; Za 5: ]73-57 , 57-54-56[; Za 6: AB 01-09-60-04 (09 dotted; revises the 1996-2000 rapport's AB 01-28-60-04); Zb 7: .-60-67-.-30-09[; Za 8: ]28-A 301-54-57 , 57-57[-.-].-.[; Za 9: 57-03-60-57-09 (60, 09 dotted); Za 10: 16-31-60-81 (81 dotted); Za 11: , 02-16[ (dotted; or ]16-02 |); Za 12: , 08-.[ (dotted); the libation formula AB 08-59-28-A 301-54-57 opens Za 1/2/3/4/8 (also Iouktas, Palaikastro, Kophinas, Troullos; Apodoulou variant AB 57-59-28-A 301-10-57)

notes: All present in silver (SYZa1-12, SYZb7); KEY DELTAS vs silver to check: Za 3 join text, Za 4 AB 48, Za 6 second sign 09-vs-28

description: NEGATIVE x2: Civitillo reviews the incised Pelikata sherds (Faure 1989: LA) concluding - like Driessen 1990 (Rapport 1986-1990 p. 446) - that they are NOT writing; the same conclusion for the Haghios Athanasios 'tablet' (Kontorli-Papadopoulou, Papadopoulos & Owens, Kadmos 44 (2005) 183-186: 'A possible linear sign from Ithaki (AB 09 SE)?')
publication: Civitillo 2008-2009, Sulle presunte 'iscrizioni' in lineare A e B da Itaca, AION N.S. 15-16, 71-87
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - not writing; correctly absent from silver

description: PUBLISHED (preliminary): the four-sign before-firing inscription on the Cretan-type jar shoulder from the House of the Ladies light-well (1990), LM IA; easily readable as AB 08-59-06-46 (hapax); comparable sequences AB 08-59-06-[.] (ZA 9.4) and AB 08-59-06-04 (ZA 10a.2) lengthen the list of apparent LA 'flexions'; palaeographic interest: the AB 06 form with two small vertical strokes above the vertical stroke is without parallel in the LA corpus
publication: Boulotis 2008, Oi pinakides Grammikis A apo to Akrotiri (THE 7-12), in Doumas (ed.) AKROTIRI THIRAS. Trianta Chronia erevnas (Library of the Athens Archaeological Society 257), 70, fig. 8
notes: Reading printed; present in silver as THEZb6 (but silver ALSO has THEZb7 - Karnava-scheme duplicate? - identity check needed)

description: PUBLISHED (preliminary, photos only - no facsimiles or transnumerations; definitive edition announced as imminent): six badly-fired tablet fragments recomposed from smaller ones (~30 tiny fragments remain unplaced), found August 1993 inside an asaminthos (bathtub) in the SW corner of room Delta 18a, Complex Delta; LM IA; possibly 2-3 original tablets at most; partial readings printed: THE 7 (opisthographic) face a last two lines = traces of a sign + numeral 7, then logogram AB 21f + numeral 46, face b numeral traces (maybe 40); THE 8 = a sign interpreted as ligature AB 54+09 (if correct, new sign A 534bis) + numeral 200[; THE 10 = isolated AB 67; THE 11 and 12 = traces maybe compatible with logogram A 302; THE 9 has no logograms (not discussed)
publication: Boulotis 2008, ibid., 67-94
notes: ABSENT from silver under THE 7-12; silver's ad-hoc THEfr.1-3 + THEtab.4-5 (five items for six fragments) are UNVERIFIED candidates for these - identity flag; definitive edition still pending through 2021

description: OLD FIND, NEW ITEM: inscription incised after firing on the base of a lamp found at Akrotiri in 1870 by Mamet & Gorceix, kept at the Ecole francaise d'Athenes (inv. V 15), local clay; object published several times without noticing the graffito (first mention Maffre 1972, BCH 96, 26 no. 33); in course of publication by Tzachili & Karnava (Minos); proposed reading AB 09-A 332 2 (A 332 dotted; identification doubtful - A 332 attested only as logogram in HT 97b and HT 107.3 and requires clockwise rotation; alternative reading AB 73 dotted 'not completely excluded', fn. 58); NUMBERING: published as Zb 15 (Karnava's Horizon scheme); the rapport adopts Zb 14 per Rapport 2001-2005 pp. 209-210
publication: Tzachili & Karnava, An inscribed lychnos base from Akrotiri, Thera, Minos (forthcoming at rapport date; appeared Minos 39 (2016) as THE Zb 15)
corpus_status: in corpus (as THEZb15); see notes (divergence/doubt flag)
notes: SILVER FOLLOWS THE EDITORS: silver has THEZb15, not Del Freo's THEZb14 (while following Del Freo for THEZb13 - mixed scheme, divergence-register candidate); round-1 row (2016-2021 recap) superseded by this fuller record

description: NEGATIVE-LEANING: Negri proposes to recognize an LA inscription (PER Zg 1) in the two signs incised on two contiguous blocks of the left jamb of Tholos 1; the signs are indeed comparable with AB 04 and AB 08, but (as Negri concedes) they may be two simple mason's marks placed side by side by chance; GORILA's decision not to include the Peristeria signs 'semble donc irreprochable'; if included at all the prefix should be Ze (stone architectural support), not Zg (fn. 62)
publication: Negri 2001-2002, Un'iscrizione L.A 'dimenticata': PER Zg 1, in Graeco-Latina Brunensia (Festschrift Bartonek), 175-177
notes: Correctly absent from silver (GORILA exclusion endorsed)

description: STATUS: during study of pottery from the recent excavations new fragments with isolated LA signs, all incised before firing, have been identified (Zurbach pers. comm.); the final publication will reorganize the epigraphic material and slightly modify the Rapport 2001-2005 numbering
publication: Zurbach pers. comm.
notes: BOOKKEEPING row; the reorganization happened: Niemeier, Del Freo & Zurbach 2015, Kadmos 54 (see Rapport 2011-2015 row)

site: Haghia Triada (Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Firenze)
description: REPUBLICATION without modifications of the nine Haghia Triada nodules with LA marks kept in Florence (already in GORILA II and CMS II 6, nos. 340-346); Jasink 2009, catalogue CR 226-CR 233
publication: Jasink 2009, La collezione di sigilli e cretule egee, in Jasink & Bombardieri (eds) Le collezioni egee del Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Firenze, 77-88, tab. 40-44
notes: BOOKKEEPING row; items already in corpus via GORILA II

description: READING DISPUTE: Christakis publishes a new photo of the inscription on the rim of pithos HM 5194; GORILA IV (unable to find the pithos, using Brice's ILA photo) read AB 07-06-10 , AB 131 17 (17 dotted); after MacGillivray REDISCOVERED the pithos in the Herakleion Museum, Olivier corrected 17 to 117 (Rapport 1986-1990 p. 446); Christakis's photo unfortunately shows strokes corresponding to the numeral 107
publication: Christakis 2010, A wine offering to the Central Palace Sanctuary at Knossos: the evidence from KN Zb 27, in Krzyszkowska (ed.) Cretan Offerings: Studies in Honour of Peter Warren, 49-56, fig. 6.4
notes: RESOLVED LATER: 107 confirmed by autopsy (Rapport 2011-2015); DIVERGENCE FLAG: silver still carries the item as KNZb<27> with angle brackets (= lost/unlocated) although the pithos was rediscovered - brackets obsolete; check silver's numeral

description: DELETED: the direct examination of the flat-based nodule HM 676 (Del Freo & Zurbach, Herakleion Museum, July 2009) EXCLUDES that the visible grooves are traces of writing - they are probably traces of simple plant ligaments (suggestion E. Fiandra per litteras 2009-08-11); 'L'inscription est donc supprimee'; the number 53 should not be reused for other documents
publication: Autopsy result reported in this rapport
notes: REMOVAL row (the item Del Freo himself had added in Rapport 2001-2005): silver correctly LACKS PHWb53; number kept vacant - hence PH 54 for the next Phaistos item (Rapport 2011-2015)

site: unknown provenance (Metropolitan Museum of New York)
description: READINGS ESTABLISHED: dark-green serpentine seal in the shape of a longitudinally-perforated spool (inv. 26.31.158, Seager Collection); possible LA signaled by Kenna 1964 (AJA 68, 9); CMS XII (1972) no. 96; CTLA (both editions) as KT[?] Z 2; GORILA excluded it as possible pseudo-writing; on Perna's photos and casts Godart & Olivier were 'perhaps too prudent': faces a and b read easily AB 28-01-01 (hapax) and AB 08-02-04 (hapax; 02 dotted - four-pointed-star vs cross shape discussed, near-absence of AB 02 on stone noted); provenance unknown; AB 08/28 forms characteristic of the Iouktas offering-tables suggest the Knossos region; chronology uncertain (pre/protopalatial seal form; face-b architectural motif attested to MM III)
publication: Kenna 1964, AJA 68, 9; CMS XII (1972) no. 96; readings from Perna's photos/casts printed in this rapport (ed.pr. Perna 2015, see Rapport 2011-2015 row)
notes: Readings printed in rapport; present in silver as CRZg4 - check silver carries AB 28-01-01 / AB 08-02-04

description: PUBLISHED: opisthographic tablet fragment (12.174) found 2012 by Watrous in Room 16 (Trench 55), destruction level dated LM IB but earlier than the final destruction; found together with inscribed roundel GO Wc 3 and several sealings; difficult to read (numerous cracks); records fractional quantities
publication: Younger in Watrous et al. 2015, Excavations at Gournia 2010-2012, Hesperia 84, 443-446, fig. 32
notes: Present in silver as sided GO2r/GO2v (round-1 sigla note); no full text printed in rapport

description: NEW: roundel (12.183, diam. ca. 2 cm) from the same context as GO 2; two seal impressions on the rim countermarked by a vertical stroke; one or more signs incised on one face; Younger: inscription traced to the RIGHT of the impressions (unusual - normally below) comprising a NEW LOGOGRAM (a circle with two superposed dots inside) followed by numerals 2 and 20 (perhaps relating to the two impressions); Del Freo alternative: a ligature of AB 80 (cf. PK 1.7) with another sign - perhaps AB 74, or AB 85 (Olivier)
publication: Younger in Watrous et al. 2015, ibid., 446-448, fig. 33
notes: ABSENT from silver - genuine gap; reading disputed (new logogram + '2' '20' vs AB 80-ligature)

description: PUBLISHED: the 2009 tablet fragment; findspot = same area as the (still inedit) roundel Wc 2124, corresponding to the findspot of LB tablet X 7 (fig. 6 of the publication); Vlazaki: KH 101 lay in a fill at a higher level than X 7; Godart assigns KH 101 to scribe 1, author of the texts from both Platia Haghia Aikaterini and the Odos Katre archive (Katre 10); the fragment contains logograms, numeric signs and fractions
publication: Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Godart 2014, Three New Linear A and B Tablets from Khania, Pasiphae 8, 11-17 (figs. 8, 10)
notes: Present in silver; scribe-1 attribution links the two Khania archives

description: PUBLISHED (preliminary): the 2010 fragment from Room M of Building 2, LM IIIB1 deposit; left part of the centre of a tablet; two fragmentary signs readable AB 08-73[ (73 dotted); the two signs are attested in the same position in AB 08-73-01-10 (ZA 10a.3), ]AB 08-73-01-61 (PH (?) 31b.5) and AB 08-73-59 (ZA 10b.4-5)
publication: Hallager, Tzedakis & Andreadaki-Vlazaki 2014, The Greek-Swedish-Danish Excavations at Kastelli, Khania 2010: A Preliminary Report, PDIA 7, 209-220 (213, 216, fig. 11)
notes: Present in silver; ed.pr. 2018 (Kadmos 57) adds alternative AB 08-65[ (round-1 row)

description: NEW + PUBLISHED: tablet fragment found 2013 during excavation of a mixed deposit of stones and animal bones south of an archaic wall crossing a Mycenaean paved court E-W; deposit considered post-earthquake, LM IIIB; records logograms of different commodities (A 302, A 303 and perhaps AB 30, AB 131 - both dotted) followed by the corresponding quantities
publication: Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Godart 2014, ibid. (figs. 9, 11); context: Andreadaki-Vlazaki 2015, Pasiphae 9, 27-42
notes: Present in silver

description: INEDIT: tablet fragment found 2014 by Hallager in a Geometric context inside Room B; left part of a tablet with two lines of writing and traces of a third
publication: Information courtesy of E. Hallager; ed.pr. later Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Hallager 2018, Kadmos 57 (round-1 row)
notes: Present in silver; ed.pr. reads fractional quantities of grain after syllabic sequences (round-1 row, incl. the rejected ligature AB 120+26)

description: INEDIT: small tablet fragment with three surviving signs, found 2014 by Hallager in an LM IIIB2 context inside the courtyard of Building 2 south of Room C
publication: Information courtesy of E. Hallager; ed.pr. later Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Hallager 2018, Kadmos 57 (round-1 row)
notes: Present in silver; ed.pr. reads AB 45-67-37[ (round-1 row)

description: AUTOPSY CONFIRMATION: after examining the inscription (15 April 2011) Del Freo & Zurbach establish that Davis's photo-based re-reading AB 67-59-30-04 (Rapport 2006-2010) is CORRECT
publication: Autopsy result reported in this rapport; cf. Davis 2008, Kadmos 47, 55-56
notes: Present in silver - check silver carries the Davis reading (not Driessen's AB 13+40-59-30-04)

description: INEDIT: fragment of an inscribed libation table found on the surface near the peak sanctuary by a student of C. Knappett, June 2012; the twelfth of its type from Petsophas (PK Za 8-12, 14-18 + Driessen 1994's PK Za 20); two sequences of 5 and 3 (maybe 4) signs: ] , AB 57-31-31-60-13 , 10-06-77-.[ (10 dotted, very uncertain) = ] , JA-SA-SA-RA-ME , U-NA-KA-.[ in LB values; last sign compatible with AB 06 (dotted) but a word-divider is not excluded; theoretical alternative AB 45 (= DE-NA-KA-...) hindered by the missing 'ears' of the sign; the formulaic sequence JA-SA-SA-RA-ME , U-NA-KA-NA-SI attested or restorable in IO Za 2c-d.1, PK Za 8b and TL Za 1b favours the first hypothesis
publication: To be published by Knappett, Del Freo & Zurbach (appeared: Knappett, Del Freo & Zurbach 2017, SMEA NS 3, 73-82 - round-1 row)
notes: Reading printed in rapport; present in silver; round-1 row (2016-2021 recap, which prints NO reading) superseded by this fuller record

description: EDITIO PRINCEPS: Hallager 2012 confirms the MM III date and the transcription (.1 AB 28-06-[.]-04 .2 AB 59-06-80-46) of the 2000 find; classification 'terracotta rod' hence the Zg prefix; findspot corrected to a refuse pit in Sector III, west of House I.1; under line 2 traces of a possible third line (original height at least 8 cm?); Hallager: coarse clay and 2.5 cm thickness exclude a tablet, cult-object association suggests votive; DEL FREO: the pinacological anomalies are not decisive and a classification as PE <6> remains possible (angle brackets because the fragment is currently unlocatable; MM II-III archive documents with similar thickness: KE 1, MA 6 at 1.90 cm, PH 28 at 1.80 cm)
publication: Hallager 2012, Literacy at Petras and three hitherto unpublished Linear A inscriptions, Monographs of the Danish Institute at Athens 16, 265-275 (267-269, fig. 3); cf. Del Freo & Zurbach 2011, BCH 135, 91 n. 75
notes: Present in silver as PEZg6 (Hallager's designation); RELOCATED 2017 in the Siteia Museum storerooms -> PE 6 (Rapport 2016-2021, round-1 row)

description: REVISED READING: the pithos SM 12069 (LM IB) was restored by the INSTAP Study Center; the inscription turns out DIFFERENT from the Colloquium Romanum version: to the left of one of the four handles the isolated sign AB 08 traced AFTER firing; to the right a group incised BEFORE firing read by Hallager AB 57-54-A 100/102-. (A 100/102 uncertain); after autopsy at the Siteia Museum Del Freo & Zurbach consider the third sign more probably a simplified variant of AB 39 (like KN (?) Wc 26); the GORILA Supplement will print AB 57-54-39-.[ (cf. AB 08-54-39 in KN Zf 31 and AB 57-54-[ in KN Za 18, whose traces after 54 seem compatible with 39)
publication: Hallager 2012, ibid., 271, fig. 4
notes: Present in silver - check which reading silver carries (Hallager's A 100/102 vs DF&Z's AB 39)

description: EXCLUSION DECISION: pithos SM 11906 (LM IB) with the isolated sign AB 08 traced before firing to the right of a handle (identical to the after-firing sign on SM 12069); Hallager: possibly logographic (cf. HT 37.5) and hence a true inscription; the GORILA Supplement will however only admit isolated signs of sure or probable logographic value (like AB 131), so this sign 'ne sera pas inclus parmi les nouvelles inscriptions' (cf. Del Freo & Zurbach 2011, 78)
publication: Hallager 2012, ibid.
notes: DIVERGENCE FLAG: silver INCLUDES PEZb8 while the GORILA Supplement will exclude it - inclusion-criteria divergence

description: NEW: tablet fragment (inv. F 8150) with two lines of writing, found summer 2013 by Militello while cleaning Room 101-1: .1 AB 28-31-53-44[ .2 ] vestigia [ (sup./inf. mut.); associated ceramic MM IIIA - same dating Militello proposes for PH 1 (found like the Phaistos Disc in Room 101-8; PH 3 and Wb 32 also MM III); NUMBERING: Phaistos numbering is continuous regardless of support; the last number, PH Wb 53 (Hallager 1999 for nodule HM 676), was shown to be plant-ligament traces (Rapport 2006-2010) and will not enter the Supplement, but the number 53 stays VACANT (contra the usual GORILA practice) to avoid confusion - hence PH 54
